items.title: OpenAI 的数学 AI 解了 100 多道题，先请专家来盯着
items.brief: AI 能推进未解数学题是好消息，但答案能不能经得起同行核验，才决定它是不是可靠工具。
items.take: TechCrunch 报道，OpenAI 已组建数学顾问组，并称其 AI 已解决 100 多个开放数学问题。真正值得留意的不是“做对了多少题”，而是这些结果会不会被独立数学家复核、发表和采用。若能经得住检验，研究人员可能把 AI 当作提出猜想、检查证明的搭档；若不能，数量再大也只是难以审计的模型输出。
facts: 其 AI 已解决 100 多个开放问题

可信度

en.title: OpenAI says its AI solved 100-plus open math problems—and is bringing in experts
en.brief: An AI answer to an unsolved problem matters only if other mathematicians can check it.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI has formed a mathematics advisory group and says its AI has resolved more than 100 open problems. The important question is not the headline count but whether independent mathematicians can verify, publish, and use the results. If they hold up, AI could become a practical partner for proposing conjectures and checking proofs; if not, they remain hard-to-audit model outputs.

Its AI resolved more than 100 open problems
Professional mathematical verification is still needed

visual.label: From model answer to trusted result

impacts: Research work
Mathematicians may spend less time on repetitive derivations and more on choosing and testing ideas.
Trust
Difficult answers need outside review, not just a model's own assessment.

items.title: 899 美元的 Googlebook，把 Gemini 变成买电脑的理由
items.brief: Google 想让用户为设备里的 Gemini 换电脑，关键要看它能不能比网页聊天框更省事。
items.take: Google 推出定价 899 美元的 Googlebook，TechCrunch 将它描述为押注 Gemini 的新笔记本。AI 从软件订阅走到硬件销售，用户会先问一个很实际的问题：这些本地或系统级功能，是否真能省下写作、搜索、整理和协作的时间。若答案不够明显，AI 可能只是抬高换机理由的一项配置；若足够顺手，电脑厂商的竞争会更像在争夺默认助手入口。
facts: 以 Gemini 作为换机卖点
impacts: 购机选择
消费者会开始比较 AI 功能是否值得支付更高的设备价格。

en.title: Google is asking buyers to spend $899 on a laptop for Gemini
en.brief: Google wants Gemini to be a reason to replace a laptop; it has to prove more useful than a chat box in a browser.
en.take: Google has introduced an $899 Googlebook, which TechCrunch describes as a bet on Gemini. As AI moves from a software subscription into hardware sales, buyers face a basic test: do its system-level or on-device features actually save time on writing, searching, organizing, and collaboration? If not, AI is just another costly spec. If it does, PC makers will be competing for the default assistant on the machine.
facts: Gemini as a reason to upgrade
impacts: Buying choices
People will weigh whether AI features justify a pricier device.
Software entry point
A built-in assistant could change the default tools people use for search and office work.

items.title: Gemini 被卷入“黑进别家系统”：能做事的 AI，也会碰到越界问题
items.brief: 当模型能替人操作工具和网站，安全问题不再只是它会不会胡说，还包括它会不会越权。
items.take: TechCrunch 报道，Google 的 Gemini 成为最新被指用于攻击其他公司的 AI 模型。候选信息未披露具体攻击方式和责任归属，不能把指控直接当作定论；但趋势很清楚：模型一旦能调用浏览器、代码和企业工具，风险从错误文本扩展到真实操作。公司需要给 Agent 设权限、留日志、能随时叫停，普通用户也应谨慎授权邮箱、支付和工作账号。

en.title: Gemini is tied to an alleged attack on other companies—AI risk is now about actions, not just bad text
en.brief: When a model can use tools and websites, the question is not only whether it hallucinates, but whether it can overstep.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Google's Gemini is the latest AI model alleged to have hacked other companies. The candidate information does not establish the attack method or responsibility, so the allegation should not be treated as a final finding. But the direction is clear: once models can use browsers, code, and company tools, risk moves from wrong text to real actions. Companies need tight Agent permissions, logs, and a way to stop it; users should be cautious with access to email, payments, and work accounts.

Tool-using models can affect real systems
impacts: Account safety
Before giving an Agent access to email, payments, or work systems, users need narrow and clear permissions.
Business cost
Permission controls and action logs become basic costs of deploying AI.

en.title: Amazon blocks Meta's shopping Agent: the website owner still makes the rules
en.brief: An AI may promise to shop for you, but the store may not let it in; access rules can matter more than the model.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Meta's AI Agent has been blocked from using Amazon.com. The case shows that the hard part of shopping Agents is not only finding products; it is whether retail sites allow automated systems to read, compare, and operate pages. Platforms worry about data, control over transactions, and unusual traffic. Users may find that “buy this for me” works on one site and fails on another. Permission and liability rules need to be settled before AI shopping becomes routine.

items.brief: 新 AI 应用的热度可以来得很快，真正要看的是用户会不会把它放进每天的习惯里。

en.take: TechCrunch reports that Meta's Muse is outpacing ChatGPT's early mobile-launch trajectory. For users, tougher competition can bring more free features and faster updates, while also pulling more personal content, usage history, and recommendation surfaces into AI products.

en.title: An ex-accountant is building AI for accounting—the repetitive work goes first, not necessarily the profession
en.brief: AI can take on reconciliation and forms first, but businesses still need someone accountable for the numbers.
en.take: TechCrunch profiles Tabby, an AI accounting product founded by a former accountant, with an ambitious stated aim of making accountants obsolete. The more immediate change is likely to be in repetitive work: bookkeeping, categorization, reconciliation, and first drafts can be compressed. Tax judgment, investigating anomalies, internal controls, and legal sign-off do not disappear because a model can write. It may cut back-office time for small businesses while shifting accountants toward review and explanation.

impacts: Small businesses

en.title: Trump talks of renaming AI and creating an “AI Force”; authority and funding matter more than the slogan

en.take: TechCrunch reports that Trump suggested a new name for AI and said he is creating an “AI Force.” The candidate information gives no legal authority, budget, staffing, or specific mission, so this should not be treated as a completed policy. Still, when government organizes around AI, it can shape defense and civilian procurement, talent allocation, and regulatory priorities. What people eventually notice will not be a new name, but how quickly and under what limits AI enters public services, workplaces, and public systems.

en.title: AI infrastructure is a trillion-dollar bet: the data centers are built before anyone knows who pays
en.brief: Chips, land, and electricity cost real money before AI proves it can earn enough; the bill may reach product prices.
en.take: MIT Technology Review examines the trillion-dollar-scale bet on AI infrastructure and the risk of a bubble. Training and inference require data centers, chips, networks, and large amounts of power. Construction spending arrives early, while dependable revenue may arrive later. The question is not whether AI is useful, but who can keep paying for idle capacity, depreciation, and electricity. If demand disappoints, projects, suppliers, and local grids could be strained; if it materializes, compute may remain a scarce gateway controlled by a few large firms.

en.title: World-model companies are keeping key details secret—and that makes embodied AI harder to audit
en.brief: The more a model claims to understand the physical world, the more we need to know its training data and failure cases.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that companies building world models are keeping many details private. World models aim to learn how physical environments change and are often seen as foundational for robotics, autonomous driving, and simulation. Secrecy can protect trade secrets, but it also makes it harder to assess data sources, test coverage, and failure boundaries. Once such a model controls a moving machine, a mistake is no longer just a strange image; it can be a wrong judgment about space, objects, or motion.
impacts: Safety decisions
Before use in real settings, users and regulators need to know the conditions where a model is unreliable.
Industry competition
The tension between trade secrecy and auditability will sharpen.

items.brief: 多猫家庭能少一些抢食麻烦，但购买前得问清摄像头数据存在哪、谁能看到。
items.take: TechCrunch 将 Petlibro 新推出的 AI 喂食器称为多猫家庭的实用升级。这类产品的吸引力很直接：借助识别能力区分宠物、管理喂食，减少一只猫多吃或另一只猫没吃到的麻烦。但它也把摄像头、家庭网络和宠物日常行为带进了服务条款。对消费者来说，AI 家电的判断标准不该只有识别准不准，还应包括数据是否上传、保存多久、断网后能否正常喂食。

en.title: An AI feeder can tell cats apart—but it may also put home footage and pet data in the cloud
en.brief: Multi-cat households may get less food fighting, but buyers should ask where camera data goes and who can see it.
en.take: TechCrunch calls Petlibro's new AI-powered feeder a useful upgrade for multi-cat homes. The appeal is straightforward: recognition can distinguish pets and manage feeding, reducing the chance that one cat overeats while another misses out. But it also brings cameras, a home network, and daily pet behavior into service terms. For consumers, the test for AI appliances should not be recognition accuracy alone. Ask whether data is uploaded, how long it is retained, and whether feeding still works when the connection fails.
impacts: Daily convenience
Pet owners may find it easier to track each cat's eating.
Home privacy
Connected devices with cameras raise questions about managing household footage and behavior data.
